frontier_source.candidate_scope: Proposed shared event-log authority using Portalocker around canonical Argus events.jsonl writers, with tail isolation and existing writer-specific semantics retained.

verified_claims: Portalocker is a Python file-locking library and documents cross-platform locking.
On Linux/Unix its locks are advisory by default.
On Windows, exclusive locks work through built-in msvcrt without the optional pywin32 dependency; shared locks require the optional win32 extra.
The documented lock pattern protects a body only when application code actually executes the Portalocker acquire/with path.

assessment.mechanism_support: The Portalocker primary source supports the local locking primitive needed by the proposed design, subject to advisory-lock semantics on POSIX and cooperation by all writers.
assessment.residual_work_protected_or_user_executor: The useful outcome still requires target application/runtime execution of patched Python code and target-environment regression tests. That executor is not eliminated by the repository/API mechanism and is not exposed by this scheduled-Chat run.
assessment.finite_monthly_trial_paid_quota_dependen: No finite monthly/trial/paid quota is inherent to the local Portalocker exclusive-lock primitive in the verified primary-source scope. This does not rescue the route because the residual executor gate already fails.
assessment.incremental_monetary_cost: No library fee is identified in the verified scope; deployment/runtime economics are not asserted. The route remains unresolved because useful execution is external to the Chat-native path.
exact_scope_limitations: This slice did not independently resolve or fetch the public Argus repository identity/commit cited by the worker artifact, so its three-writer inventory is not independently re-verified here.
No runtime concurrency, crash-tail, rotation, unlock-failure, or migration-contention test was executed.
POSIX advisory locking does not itself prevent non-cooperating writers.
assessment.acceptance_effect: Do not count this candidate as Phase-1 dependency-elimination acceptance evidence. Treat Portalocker as a plausible implementation primitive only after a separate Chat-native mechanism eliminates or directly exposes the target execution/deployment path.
